subject: Municipal Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Role
overview: Medford Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Director Frances Nwajei discussed the scope and mechanics of municipal DEI work, internal collaboration across city departments, and the distinctions between allyship and co-disrupting. No official municipal votes or formal actions took place during the interview.

items.title: Introduction and Medford Favorites
items.summary: Director Frances Nwajei introduced herself, detailed her role and office location in City Hall, and discussed local dining.

items.title: The Evolution and Mechanics of DEI Work
items.summary: Nwajei explained the roots of DEI in affirmative action and civil rights compliance, emphasizing that meaningful systemic change requires realistic timelines and structural commitment rather than reactionary responses.

items.title: Medford Initiatives and Police Collaboration
items.summary: Nwajei shared her experiences working with Medford's Social Justice Roadmap, the Office of Prevention and Outreach, and the police department on training and diverse hiring.

items.title: Allyship Versus Co-Disrupting
items.summary: Nwajei distinguished between surface-level allyship and active co-disrupting, stressing the need for real intervention, tangible support, and setting achievable goals.

items.title: Supporting the DEI Office
items.summary: Nwajei requested that the community engage with her work authentically and understand that the role is both personal and professional rather than political.
